thread:
sara: Quick check-in — can we clarify operator vs central scheduler boundary for handling transient admission tokens (burst lane)? struggling to map failure modes.
jon: Are you talking about the token that grants ephemeral GPU slots for a request? RFC had a few options but not a hard call.
alex: TL;DR from the RFC: two extremes — operator-authoritative (operator mints/validates tokens) vs central-authoritative (scheduler hands out tokens, operator enforces). each has tradeoffs: latency vs global accounting.
mike: my take: keep admission path local for latency: operator checks a short-lived LeaseRequest and returns LeaseResponse. central reconciler still holds global quotas and periodically reconciles ledger.
mike: small API sketch:
```
LeaseRequest { tenant_id: string, desired_gpus: int, ttl_sec: int }
LeaseResponse { granted: bool, lease_id: string?, expires_at: int?, reason: string? }
```
sara: ok but who owns uniqueness/anti-replay and cross-operator double-spend?
jon: central should be the source of truth for long-term quotas. we can use optimistic local grants with a soft hold: operator grants a short TTL, then central does a fast check-in to convert to a committed reservation. if central rejects, operator preempts.
maria: compliance note: any conversion to committed reservation must emit an audit event (tenant, lease_id, actor:central/operator). we need consistent IDs.
alex: failure modes: network partition — operator could keep serving based on local short TTLs and then revoke if central later fails the commit. that keeps latency but risks temporary overcommit. mitigation: conservative TTLs + headroom safety.
sara: what about backpressure signals? operator should expose metrics: local_grants, revocations, commit_latency, failed_commits. central uses these for admission throttling.
mike: agree. also suggest an explicit fallback path: if central is unreachable, operator should stop granting beyond soft headroom and route excess to queued admission with tokenless backoff.
jon: also important: API contract must include an idempotency key for LeaseRequest so retries don't double-grant. and include a required nonce signed by operator when committing.
maria: encryption/audit: lease_id and nonce format should be deterministic and human-unfriendly (no PII). store in KMS-backed secrets for verification.
sara: runbook snippet idea:
- detect commit_failure_rate > 1% => flip operator to strict mode (no optimistic grants)
- commit_latency > 200ms => increase local TTL and alert SRE
- central unreachable => degrade to queued admission and publish status to /status page

mike: i'll draft a short follow-up RFC with the API + failure semantics. can one of you own the ledger reconciliation section? jon?
jon: happy to take ledger reconciliation and metrics contract.
sara: thanks — mike + jon pair on RFC. i'll schedule a 30m sync Thurs to go over edge cases. adding action items: mike write RFC, jon ledger + metrics, alex ops failure scenarios, maria audit spec.
mike: will put a draft in docs and ping here when ready. :thumbsup:
